relevance_note: Single-patient case report of LAD with a CD18 (ITGB2) variant: 'A patient with a severe LAD phenotype was studied and the molecular basis of the disease was identified as a single homozygous defect'.
method_note: Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a small Python script from hand-chosen values and checked every span against the Markdown. One in-scope person (the single case-report patient, label 'patient'). Table 1 lists CD18 mutations from earlier reports by codon/reference, not individuals; no patient-level facts (sex, age, features) are given, so no rows were created for it. Parents are not described beyond 'father was not known' and 'No genetic material from the parents was available'; no relative rows. Consanguinity recorded 'not reported' because the paper says only 'consanguinity of the parents was suspected'. Variant printed as legacy description; 'x37' is printed as such (likely a rendering of a minus sign) and kept verbatim; no HGVS, transcript or genomic coordinates printed. variant_type set to 'other' (authors call it a genomic deletion of 169 bp spanning the intron 4 acceptor site and exon 5, causing exon 5 skipping and an in-frame 171-nt mRNA deletion); it could also be read as splice or in-frame. Homozygosity is stated by the authors and supported by competitive PCR (two copies). Age at diagnosis taken from 'laboratory findings at 7months were consistent with a severe LAD diagnosis'. Deceased age from 'deceased 1-year-old male'; age at last evaluation left not reported. 'CSF infection with Staphylococcus simulans' not mapped to the meningitis checklist item because the paper does not call it meningitis. Functional data on the HVS-transformed T-cell line are in functional_evidence_statement, not phenotypic_features. No contradictions found.

functional_evidence_statement.value: cDNA from the patient's HVS T-cell line showed a 171-nucleotide in-frame deletion (total skipping of exon 5); no CD18 on the cell surface or in the cytoplasm of the patient's HVS T-cell line (null vs 97000 molecules per cell in control); null CD11a/CD18 on peripheral lymphocytes; HVS T cells showed severely impaired proliferation to CD2 stimulation not corrected by IL-2
span: DNA sequencing of the amplified cDNA demonstrated a 171-nucleotide deletion corresponding to the total absence of exon 5 (from 329 to 500bp).
The 171-bp shortened 'inframe' mRNA not only resulted in the absence of CD18 expression on the cell surface but also in its absence in the cytoplasm of HVS T-cell lines.

Quantitative analysis of the exact number of CD18 molecules per cell with an anti-CD18 mAb revealed a null expression of CD18 in the LAD-HVS cell line compared with 97000 molecules per cell in the CT-HVS cell line
flow cytometry analysis of the CD11a/CD18 integrin complex showed a null expression of this molecule in the PBMCs of the patient

revealed a normal proliferative response of LAD cells to all mitogens, but that of CD2 was severely impaired, with a fivefold reduction when compared to controls. This poor response of the patient's T cells to CD2 was not corrected by the addition of exogenous IL-2.
